entries.25af315fe9111a8d: The main products are powertrain-related products that transmit the power of engines and motors to the wheels (automatic transmissions, hybrid transmissions, eAxle, and others), and driving safety-related products that stop the vehicle (disc brakes, electric parking brakes, and others). In addition, there are body-related products such as doors and sunroofs, LBS-related and other products such as car navigation systems, and aftermarket-related products that are repair and maintenance products. Products not installed in vehicles include energy solutions-related products such as gas heat pump air conditioners (GHP) and cogeneration systems, and femtosecond fiber lasers. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, external revenue from "Energy solutions-related and other" was ¥126,260 million. The company lists "combining its hardware strengths, such as powertrain units and brakes, with sensing and software" as a key initiative in its 2028 medium-term management plan.

entries.f3c2a799caebec77: It was founded as Tokai Hikoki Co., Ltd. with capital of ¥50 million through joint investment by Toyota Motor Industries Corporation (now [[company:toyota|Toyota Motor]] Corporation) and Kawasaki Aircraft Co., Ltd. (currently Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Ltd.). In March 1944, the Kariya Plant was completed, and it made aircraft engine parts until the end of the war. At the end of 1945, it switched to manufacturing sewing machines and automotive parts, changed its company name to Aichi Kogyo Co., Ltd. in December of the same year, and in June 1949, upon receiving approval for a reorganization plan under the Enterprise Reconstruction and Reorganization Act, it was launched as the new Aichi Kogyo Co., Ltd. with capital of ¥15 million. What the annual securities report prints as "founding" is this June 1949.

For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥544,258 million, segment profit was ¥69,618 million, the second largest after Japan, and the number of employees was 17,599. The company explains that revenue and profit increased because of higher vehicle production volume at customers and higher sales volume of powertrain units, in addition to the continued trend of a weaker yen.

For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥566,074 million, segment profit was ¥30,657 million and the number of employees was 13,020. The company explains that revenue decreased because of lower sales volume of automatic transmissions, and that profit decreased also because of one-time costs such as structural reform expenses.
